title: The Frogs Who Desired a King
summary: The frogs of a wide, fertile marsh lived in blissful freedom, leaping through the reeds, sunning themselves on water lilies, and croaking in noisy chorus whenever they pleased. But...
keywords: the frogs who desired a king
full_text:
The frogs of a wide, fertile marsh lived in blissful freedom, leaping through the reeds, sunning themselves on water lilies, and croaking in noisy chorus whenever they pleased. But over time, they grew dissatisfied with their orderly liberty. "Every kingdom on earth has a sovereign to rule over them," they argued. "Why should we be a leaderless rabble? We need a king to maintain majesty and govern our pond!"

They sent a solemn petition to the heavens, begging for a king to rule over them.

Amused by their foolishness, Jupiter tossed a colossal wooden log down into the center of the swamp. It struck the water with a tremendous splash: CRASH! The frogs, terrified by the thunderous impact, scattered beneath the mud, hiding in the dark depths for hours, convinced that their new king was a terrifying titan.

Gradually, seeing the monarch neither moved nor spoke, a bold frog poked his head above the water. Seeing only an inert piece of timber floating among the duckweed, the frogs swam closer. Within an hour, they were leaping onto the log, sunning on its bark, and mocking its total silence.

"This is no king!" they croaked in indignation. "It is a lifeless, contemptible stick! We demand a dynamic, vigorous ruler who commands respect and takes action!"

Wearied by their incessant complaining, Jupiter sent them a tall, long-legged Water Stork.

The moment the new sovereign landed in the marsh, he strode through the shallows with his sharp, spear-like beak, gobbling down the frogs one by one! The terrified survivors hid in deep crevices, weeping and praying to have their gentle log returned. But the heavens answered: "You rejected peaceful freedom and despised a gentle ruler; now you must endure the tyrant you so foolishly demanded."
moral: Be careful what you wish for; discontent with freedom often invites cruel tyranny.
